He played [[college basketball]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. Thornwell was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 48th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] before he was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. ==High school career== Thornwell attended [[Lancaster High School (Lancaster, South Carolina)|Lancaster High School]] in Lancaster, South Carolina for his first three years of high school. He then transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] for his senior year where he averaged 26.8 points per game and averaged 8.6 rebounds and 3.6 assists as well. He led them to a 33–5 record. He was ranked as the 39th-best player by ESPN.com and a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], who also ranked him as the 11th-best shooting guard in his class. He also competed in the 2012 [[Nike Global Challenge]] playing in four games. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2013}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Sindarius Thornwell | position = Guard | hometown = Lancaster, South Carolina | highschool = [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 205 | 40 = | commitdate = 10/2/12 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn grade = 92 | espn stars = 4 | grayshirt = }} |} ==College career== After committing to South Carolina on October 2, 2012, Thornwell was second on the South Carolina basketball team in scoring with 13.4 ppg and 4.0 rebounds per game. He also averaged 3.0 assists per game. During conference play, he was averaging 15.0 ppg as well. On January 22, 2014, Thornwell had a career-high 26 points against the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|University of Georgia]].{{cite web | title=Georgia throttles Gamecocks | website=Garnet And Black Attack |publisher=SB Nation| date=2014-01-22 | url=https://www.garnetandblackattack.com/2014/1/22/5336768/gamecock-basketball-georgia-final-score-97-76 | access-date=2025-08-03}} As a result of his production that season, Thornwell was named a member of the All-SEC Freshman Team. His sophomore year in the [[2014–15 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|2014–15 season]] was not as productive as his freshman season. His junior year, on the other hand, would provide relatively similar results to what he had in his freshman year.{{cite web|url=http://www.gamecocksonline.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/sindarius_thornwell_851955.html|publisher=gamecocksonline.com|title=Sindarius Thornwell Bio University of South Carolina Official Athletic Site|access-date=April 11, 2017}} However, it would be his senior season where Thornwell would come into his own as a player, as Thornwell would average 21.4 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.2 steals in 34.2 minutes of action per game. As a result of his production that season, he was not only a member of the All-SEC First Team, but he was also named the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] thanks to votes from the coaches of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. Furthermore, Thornwell would be the main leader to help the No. 7 seeded South Carolina proceed all the way to the Final Four in the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2017 NCAA tournament]], which was the highest results in South Carolina's history. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2017–2019)=== On June 22, 2017, Thornwell was selected with the 48th pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], but his draft rights were then traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|title=L.A. Clippers acquire rights to Sindarius Thornwell|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/06/23/la-clippers-acquire-rights-sindarius-thornwell|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 11, 2018|date=June 22, 2017}} Thornwell signed with the Clippers on July 26.{{cite web|title=Press Release: L.A. CLIPPERS SIGN SINDARIUS THORNWELL|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-clippers-sign-sindarius-thornwell-170726|website=Los Angeles Clippers|access-date=October 11, 2018|date=July 26, 2017}} ===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2019–2020)=== On August 4, 2019, Thornwell signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and played in three preseason games before he was waived on October 16. On October 26, 2019, the [[Canton Charge]] traded Thornwell to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] for a first-round [[G-League]] pick in 2020.{{cite web |title=VIPERS FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER |url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/vipers-finalize-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 9, 2019 |date=October 27, 2019}} Thornwell averaged 9.2 points, 5.2
